title: No nonnegative mixture of 20 published North Pacific model runs fits all eight AOU change ranges
abstract: We test joint agreement of a published near-outcrop ventilation model with eight North Pacific AOU changes on sigma0 26.5. We allow all nonnegative mixtures and unrestricted positive scaling of frozen model runs. No mixture fits all published marginal 95 percent ranges. The eight fixed-flow, uniform-use runs need a minimum equal expansion of 5.8954 umol/kg at every range edge. The eight depth-dependent-use runs need 1.5368; four changing-flow runs need 1.8061. All 20 runs together need 0.8505. Exact rational separating certificates verify these lower bounds on the published decimal inputs. In the broadest cone, the other seven targets require a WEST gain of at least 22.3963, above its published upper limit of 20.49. Removing WEST or TZ permits a fit; removing any other single region does not. The result strengthens an earlier single-scale pattern test and shows why agreement at ALOHA alone does not validate the spatial response. This is an exploratory test of finite published model outputs, not new observations or a statistical rejection of the outcrop mechanism. Sparse cruises, marginal uncertainty ranges, model structure and finite ensemble coverage limit inference. Code, aggregate inputs, primal solutions and independent certificate checks are included.

display.caption: Equal interval expansion needed by each model cone and the nearest prediction from all 20 published runs. Intervals are published marginal 95 percent ranges. Their joint use is a deterministic diagnostic, not a 95 percent test.
